prompt: Parse version tags like "v2.0.0-beta.1" with NAMED capture groups, pulling out major, minor, patch and an optional label by name rather than by number.
explanation: Named groups, written (?<name>...), let you read a match with m.group("major") instead of counting parentheses, which keeps the code readable when the pattern grows an optional suffix. Wrapping the label part in (?:-(?<label>...))? makes it a non-capturing optional wrapper around a capturing group, so a tag with no label still matches and group("label") simply returns null. Anchoring with ^ and $ -- or equivalently using matches() rather than find() -- is what rejects strings with extra characters around the tag.
hints: Start from ^v(?<major>\d+)\.(?<minor>\d+)\.(?<patch>\d+) and remember that a literal dot must be escaped as \\. in a Java string.
Make the suffix optional with (?:-(?<label>[A-Za-z0-9.]+))? -- the ?: keeps the wrapper from capturing anything itself.
m.group("label") returns null when the optional part did not match, so test for null before appending it.
